library(tidymarkers)

## What KASP is and why libraries do everything, not us

KASP (Kompetitive Allele-Specific PCR) is a point test: two allele-specific
primers (AS1/AS2) with different fluorophores and one common primer (COM).
Discrimination rests on **one** base at the 3' end of the AS primer, so the
quality of the design decides everything. The package builds the design from
proven libraries:

| Step | Library |
|-----|------------|
| Tm (nearest-neighbour) | `TmCalculator` |
| Allelic discrimination (hybridisation + Taq) | `DECIPHER` |
| Hairpins and dimers (DNA, OligoArrayAux) | wrappers `oligo_dg()` / `terminal_dg()` |
| Specificity | `Biostrings` (`PDict`, `matchProbePair`), `rBLAST` |

## Quick start

The example target table ships with the package - no network and no genome:

```{r}
marker_example()
```

The reaction recipe (`AS:AS:COM = 2:2:5`) is pure arithmetic:

```{r}
kasp_mix_recipe(n_reactions = 96)
```

## Variant classification and masking

```{r}
variant_type("G", "A")          # SNP
variant_type("A", "AGG")        # insertion
variant_type("AGG", "A")        # deletion

# replace other variants under the primer with N (so they are not carried into the primer)
mask_positions("ACGTACGT", c(2, 5))
```

## Design on your own genome

The full cycle reads a genome (TAIR10 or any FASTA) and variants (VCF or Ensembl),
so it is shown here as code (the heavy steps are not run when the document is
built):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
genome <- ath_genome()                                  # TAIR10, cached
gene   <- ensembl_gene("AT4G00650")                     # FRI
variants <- ensembl_variants(gene$chrom, gene$start, gene$end)

snp <- pick_target_snp(variants, genome, gene)
assay <- assemble_kasp_assay(genome, snp, variants = variants,
                             strands = c("+", "-"), tm_range = c(58, 64))
assay                                                   # prints a summary
passes_all(assay)                                       # TRUE / FALSE
marker_design_checks(assay)                               # row by row, what and why
```

Your own FASTA/VCF - same way, but through the input readers:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
genome <- read_genome_fasta("my.fa", seqids = c("chr1", "chr2"))  # Rsamtools index
variants <- read_variants_vcf("my.vcf.gz", chrom = "chr1")        # vroom, streaming
```

## Batch design

For hundreds of loci - a table with a verdict per locus (one bad locus does not
sink the run):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
loci <- marker_example()[c("chrom", "pos", "ref", "alt")]
design_kasp_markers(genome, loci)   # pass / warn / fail + reason
```

## Results and ordering

```{r, eval = FALSE}
write_kasp_results(assay, gene)     # marker_design.csv, marker_primer_qc.csv, marker_dimer_dg.csv,
                                    # + IDT/LGC/tidy as column subsets
```

See also `?marker_design_checks`, `?assemble_kasp_assay`, `?kasp_mix_recipe`.
